schema_note: First outbound set of the reciprocal leg. Exercises the aps-receipt-v1 TRANSPORT layer: RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization, domain-separated receipt_id, domain-separated Ed25519 receipt signatures, and closed-schema validation. It asserts nothing about APS receipt semantics and nothing about any production issuer.
integrity_convention: receipt_len + receipt_sha256 over utf8 of the COMPACT JSON serialization of the receipt in the member order as published, hex. Not over the canonical form.

profile.signer_key_resolution: Explicit inline key table below, keyed by (signer, key_id). The shipped verifier takes a resolveKey(signer, key_id, issued_at) callback returning a raw 32-byte lowercase-hex Ed25519 public key, so there is no did:key derivation inside receipt-core. The did:key form of each key is published alongside the hex so an existing did:key resolver derives the identical 32 bytes.
profile.key_custody: Both private halves derive from published seeds and are burned test keys. Neither is a production APS signer and neither appears in any other aeoess corpus.
profile.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JCS. Keys sorted at serialization time by UTF-16 code unit. No whitespace. Lone surrogates are rejected rather than escaped.
profile.scalars: String-only in this round, except evidence_refs member counts. No JSON numbers, booleans or nulls appear in any signed body, so JCS number canonicalization is out of scope for round 1.
profile.signature: value = lowercase-hex(Ed25519-Sign(key, ASCII("APS-RECEIPT-SIG-V1") || 0x00 || UTF8(JCS(signature_form)))) where signature_form = {"receipt": receipt without signatures, "signer": {signer, key_id, alg}}. The signature form INCLUDES receipt_id.
profile.receipt_id: receipt_id = lowercase-hex(SHA-256(ASCII("APS-RECEIPT-ID-V1") || 0x00 || UTF8(JCS(receipt without receipt_id and signatures)))).
profile.delegation_chain_root: delegation_chain_root = lowercase-hex(SHA-256(UTF8(JCS(chain)))). Bare: no domain tag, no separator byte. Deliberately NOT domain-separated while receipt_id is. Not a member of the aps-receipt-v1 envelope.
profile.evaluation_order: schema validation -> receipt_id recomputation -> key resolution -> signature. receipt_id BEFORE signature, per draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 section 5.2, which is the reverse of the agentlair-receipt-vectors-v1 order. Verification does NOT short-circuit after the first failure: every applicable check runs and every failure is reported.
profile.failure_code_note: Read out of src/v2/receipt-core/receipt.ts and jcs.ts at the commit named in SOURCE.md. These are the literal strings the verifier emits. There is no symbolic enum and no INVALID_CLAIM_TYPE code: a wrong profile surfaces as "ReceiptV1: profile".
profile.result_shape: Object: {valid: boolean, receipt_id_valid: boolean, signature_results: [...], errors: [string]}. A boolean plus an error list, NOT the four-value valid / invalid / indeterminate / unsupported result that draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 section 3.3 specifies. That gap is open and is disclosed here because it was disclosed in writing on 2026-07-29 and has not closed since.

keys.role: issuer verification method k1. Signed every valid vector.
issuer verification method k2. Registered to the same issuer and resolvable, but its private half never signed anything in this corpus.

profile.key_id_note: key_id is opaque to the verifier and is resolved through the table above. The did_key column gives the did:key encoding of the same 32 public bytes, so an existing did:key resolver can confirm it derives the identical key material.

vectors.vector_note: Baseline. receipt_id recomputes and the issuer signature verifies against key A.

delegation_ref mutated AFTER signing. Two errors, not one: receipt_id covers every member except receipt_id and signatures, so a content mutation breaks the id as well as the signature, and this verifier does not short-circuit. Compare receipt-2026-07-29-sig-invalid, which reports SIGNATURE_INVALID alone because that profile evaluates the signature first and stops.
Signature VALID over this exact envelope, including the wrong declared receipt_id. Only the id fails to recompute. Single fault, directly comparable to receipt-2026-07-29-receipt-id-mismatch.

key_id names key B, a well-formed Ed25519 key that did not sign. signer stays the issuer so the issuer-signature rule still holds. receipt_id is unaffected because it excludes signatures, so this is a clean single-fault signature failure.

Byte-identical content to the valid vector, transmitted with reversed member order. Verifies ONLY if canonicalization sorts at serialization time. Note receipt_sha256 differs from the valid vector while the canonical bytes and the signature are identical.

Worked delegation_chain_root example. root = lowercase-hex(SHA-256(UTF8(JCS(chain)))), computed over the chain array ALONE. No domain tag and no 0x00 separator, which is the opposite of receipt_id and is deliberate rather than an oversight. Any future correction arrives as an explicitly versioned construction, never as a silent substitution under the same name. delegation_chain_root is NOT a member of the aps-receipt-v1 envelope: it lives on the v1 PolicyReceipt and on the v2 accountability and instruction-provenance records. The receipt here is the baseline valid receipt, unchanged; the chain and its root are carried beside it so the construction can be reproduced without inventing a field the closed receipt schema would reject.
